description:
Execution boundary: planning approved; this issue does not authorize commits, pushes, merges, upstream publication, GitHub comments, live WhatsApp access, or real messages. Revalidate current source/Git state before implementation. Preserve unrelated work, including the already-edited docs/architecture.md. Track this work in the ZAQ Beadwork store even when files belong to the sibling package; do not initialize another store.
Read AGENTS.md in the affected repository. For ZAQ read docs/agent-tools.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/conventions.md and docs/code-quality.md plus the domain policies listed below. Read module documentation before editing. Source navigation uses Serena with bounded fallback if unavailable. Record test results honestly; plan approval is not completed-feature UX approval. Follow repository validation owners; no assertion weakening or unrelated refactors. Existing test changes outside the specifically approved contracts need human approval.

Required domain policies: docs/services/engine.md; docs/services/channels.md; docs/services/system-config.md; docs/architecture.md NodeRouter; docs/testing-approach.md process/isolation sections.

Functional specifications covered with associated files to edit/add:
ZAQ cross-service lifecycle invariant owner: ConnectorLifecycle (lib/zaq/engine/connector_lifecycle.ex) plus the existing Channels runtime ownership/guard in bridge_supervisor.ex and its explicit role events. This cohesive step crosses those files because the exclusion lifetime spans both roles; splitting ownership into unrelated fixes would leave a credential resurrection gap. Reuse existing start/stop serialization work zaq-0l7.21 before extending its scope.
The critical section must cover selected connector runtime preparation, logout/offline cleanup, revalidated disable persistence and runtime shutdown. Merely locking individual start/stop calls is insufficient: a start must not read enabled=true before commit and begin writing after cleanup. Recheck persisted eligibility/revision at the appropriate authority and fence stale prepared starts/handles. Every relevant startup route (bootstrap, explicit enable/retry, saved pairing activation) must honor exclusion. Do not hold a Repo row lock/DB transaction while calling Channels or an adapter: cleanup callbacks synchronously return to Engine. Do not introduce a domain->Action->same-domain recursion or cross-service lock deadlock.
Before production edits record the concrete lock/guard owner, acquisition order, cross-node semantics, release on caller death/timeout, stale-start invalidation, and exact events in this issue; prove with deterministic tests. Approved design requires existing ownership boundaries; if that cannot satisfy the invariant without a new coordinator/schema/security contract, stop and propose that deviation rather than inventing one.
Both disable and disable-before-archive reuse the same preparation/cleanup semantics from zaq-e5z.5. Success clears only selected profile; persist enabled=false only after cleanup acknowledgment; Archive only after runtime stop acknowledgment. Keep association, already-disabled idempotence, revision conflict behavior, post-persistence runtime-pending/retry semantics and watch teardown ordering. Cleanup failure leaves operation incomplete; durable clearing followed by RAM/persistence failure cannot be rolled back, report honestly and support explicit retry. Missing listener alone is not failure. No automatic success when required storage unavailable and no restoration of cleared credentials.
Missing binding/corrupt/revoked credential cases fail closed without provisioning. Local deletion cannot promise remote WhatsApp unlink. No broad permission changes beyond already authorized operations.

Tests to add before implementation:
Before edits reproduce failed activation -> saved enabled connector/no listener -> Disable and Archive; then add deterministic barrier-based races for start during cleanup, start with stale preloaded config, cleanup completed before disabled commit, retry/bootstrap/pairing-start overlap, actor/revision changes, caller exit/timeouts and guard release. Include real NodeRouter->Channels->adapter->Engine document callbacks proving no lock deadlock. Test durable-success/RAM-failure and explicit retry, shutdown failure after disabled persistence, repeated disable/archive, sibling isolation and preserved watches. Preserve existing tests in engine/connector_lifecycle_test.exs, engine/disable_channel_connector_test.exs and channels/linked_device/connector_disable_test.exs. Property tests for scope/idempotence/fencing where tractable. New browser scenarios deferred to zaq-0l7.8.

Branches/paths validated:
Listener absent/running, activation failed, success/partial cleanup failure, stale revision/start, concurrent retry/enable, owner death/timeouts, already disabled/archived, runtime stop pending, other profile unaffected.

Mocking plan:
Real internal roles, transactions, callback paths and runtime supervisor; external transport offline. Synchronization barriers/monitors instead of sleeps. Inject existing opts dependencies; isolated BEAM for global runtime/Mnesia tests. Do not satisfy concurrency tests with disconnected mocks.

Documentations to update for both code and docs/ related content:
Update ConnectorLifecycle @moduledoc to include lifecycle exclusion, docs/services/channels.md and docs/services/engine.md failure ordering/retry contract, and narrow architecture additions only if needed. Preserve the already-corrected supervision paragraph. Record lock protocol and failure traces in Beadwork.

Action reuse assessment:
Decision: extend ConnectorLifecycle plus existing per-runtime Channels serialization; reuse DisableChannelConnector, archive event, ConnectorLifecycle.context/revision/persist/sync, Channels prepare-disable/logout, Connect.CredentialDocuments and package cleanup. Existing start lock alone and a direct grant revoke both miss cross-service lifetime guarantees. Lifecycle control is local infrastructure/domain orchestration under existing confidential Events, not a new agent tool. Input exact scoped/revisioned connector + actor -> ID/status/runtime result or stage error. Credential effects may precede disable commit; no atomicity claim across stores. Tests prove all affected consumers use the shared ordered flow.

comments.text: Concrete protocol before editing: extend existing global locking with a shared connector-ID LifecycleLock helper under ConnectorConfig namespace, no new runtime service/schema. Engine holds connector lock (across connected BEAM nodes) over fresh scope/revision read, logout/offline cleanup, disable transaction and final runtime stop. A private requester token propagates only through confidential internal Channels event opts so RPC callbacks can share the lock; same-process nesting skips reacquisition to avoid prematurely releasing outer lock. Lock holder death is handled by OTP global monitoring. Lock order: connector -> existing per-runtime lock; never hold DB row transaction across service callbacks. Bound saved-runtime startup takes same connector lock before specs/credential preparation and revalidates current enabled/nonarchived Engine snapshot via explicit confidential runtime-context event. Stale preloaded configs fail after disable. Running adapter logout is followed by stopping worker/transport and final idempotent cleanup before disable persistence, so all old writers are quiesced before final clear. Ordinary stop still retains records. Credential callbacks do not acquire connector lock (avoids Engine/Channels storage deadlock). Existing guard bypass is confined to configs without saved credential document, which have no persisted linked-device binding to clean. Test token-sharing across separate processes, exclusion through commit/stop, stale starts and failure/owner-death release. Partitions do not get a new quorum guarantee.

Implemented connector lifecycle exclusion across cleanup, final stopped-writer clear, disabled persistence and runtime reconciliation. Bound startup takes same connected-node lock and resolves fresh Engine eligibility. Same-process and RPC nesting retain outer hold; owner death releases. Unbound callback fixtures retain prior listener contract. Validation: mix q passed; isolated lifecycle/supervisor/real storage subset 77 tests + 1 property passed. Deterministic barrier holds operation after real cleanup before persist; concurrent stale start blocks then fails connector_unavailable. Internal runtime-context capability denial covered. No application commit.
